source_text: Τοὺς μὲν οὖν θαυμαστὸν οὐδὲν λογοποιεῖν περὶ ἡμῶν ἃ περὶ τῶν σφετέρων λέγουσι θεῶν· καὶ τὰ πάθη αὐτῶν δεικνύουσι μυστήρια. Χρῆν δ᾿ αὐτούς, εἰ δεινὸν τὸ ἐπ᾿ ἀδείας καὶ ἀδιαφόρως μίγνυσθαι κρίνειν ἔμελλον, ἢ τὸν Δία μεμισηκέναι, ἐκ μητρὸς μὲν Ῥέας θυγατρὸς δὲ Κόρης πεπαιδοποιημένον, γυναικὶ δ᾿ ἰδίᾳ ἀδελφῇ χρώμενον, ἢ τὸν τούτων ποιητὴν Ὀρφέα, ὅτι καὶ ἀνόσιον ὑπὲρ τὸν Θυέστην καὶ μιαρὸν ἐποίησε τὸν Δία· καὶ γὰρ οὗτος τῇ θυγατρὶ κατὰ χρησμὸν ἐμίγη, βασιλεῦσαι θέλων καὶ ἐκδικηθῆναι. Ἡμεῖς δὲ τοσοῦτον ἀδιάφοροι εἶναι ἀπέχομεν, ὡς μηδὲ ἰδεῖν ἡμῖν πρὸς ἐπιθυμίαν ἐξεῖναι. Ὁ γὰρ βλέπων, φησί, γυναῖκα πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτῆς, ἤδη μεμοίχευκεν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ. Οἷς οὖν μηδὲν τὸ πλέον ἔξεστιν ὁρᾶν ἢ ἐφ᾿ ἃ ἔπλασεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὁ θεός, ἡμῖν φῶς αὐτοὺς εἶναι, καὶ οἷς τὸ ἰδεῖν ἡδέως μοιχεία, ἐφ᾿ ἕτερα τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν γεγονότων, μέχρις ἐννοίας κριθησομένοις, πῶς ἂν οὗτοι ἀπιστηθεῖεν σωφρονεῖν; Οὐ γὰρ πρὸς ἀνθρωπικοὺς νόμους ὁ λόγος ἡμῖν, οὓς ἄν τις γενόμενος πονηρὸς καὶ λάθοι (ἐν ἀρχῇ δὲ ὑμῖν, δεσπόται, θεοδίδακτον εἶναι τὸν καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς λόγον ἐπιστούμην), ἀλλ᾿ ἔστιν ἡμῖν νόμος ὃς δικαιοσύνης μέτρον ἐποίησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ τοὺς πέλας ἔχειν. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ καθ᾿ ἡλικίαν τοὺς μὲν υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας νοοῦμεν, τοὺς δὲ ἀδελφοὺς ἔχομεν καὶ ἀδελφάς, καὶ τοῖς προβεβηκόσι τὴν τῶν πατέρων καὶ μητέρων τιμὴν ἀπονέμομεν. Οὓς οὖν ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφὰς καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ τοῦ γένους νοοῦμεν ὀνόματα, περὶ πολλοῦ ἡμῖν ἀνύβριστα καὶ ἀδιάφθορα αὐτῶν τὰ σώματα μένειν, πάλιν ἡμῖν λέγοντος τοῦ λόγου· Ἐάν τις διὰ τοῦτο ἐκ δευτέρου καταφιλήσῃ, ὅτι ἤρεσεν αὐτῷ· καὶ ἐπιφέροντος· Οὕτως οὖν ἀκριβώσασθαι τὸ φίλημα μᾶλλον δὲ τὸ προσκύνημα δεῖ, ὡς, εἴπου μικρὸν τῇ διανοίᾳ παραθολωθείη, ἔξω ἡμᾶς τῆς αἰωνίου τιθέντος ζωῆς.
pass_a_gloss: They then nothing wonderful to tell about us what they say about their own gods; and they show their passions mysteries. It was necessary for them, if they were going to judge the thing on freedom and indiscriminately mixing, either to hate Zeus, who was made a boy from Rhea his mother and Kore his daughter, and using his own sister as a woman, or Orpheus who made him, because he also made Zeus unholy beyond Thyestes and polluted; for this one also mixed with his daughter according to an oracle, wanting to reign and take revenge. But we refrain from being so indifferent, as not even to be allowed to look at something with desire. For the one who looks, he says, at a woman to desire her, has already committed adultery in his heart. To whom nothing more is allowed to be seen than what God created the eyes for, for us to be light, and for whom to see adulteries with pleasure, having become other than the eyes, until the thoughts are judged, how would these people be unbelieving to be self-controlled? For the word to us is not towards human laws, which anyone becoming evil can evade (but in the beginning, I was testifying to you, masters, that the word among us is taught by God), but there is a law for us which made a measure of righteousness for them and for those around them. Because of this, we also think of sons and daughters according to age, and we have brothers and sisters, and to those who have advanced, we give the honor of fathers and mothers. Whom we think of as brothers and sisters and the rest of the family, names, it remains for us very important and their bodies unharmed, again the word tells us: If anyone kisses a second time because it pleased him; and adding: Thus then it is necessary to be precise about the kiss, or rather the greeting, so that, if the mind is slightly darkened, it puts us outside of eternal life.

pass_b_english: The pagans tell no remarkable stories about us comparable to what they tell about their own gods; indeed, their myths expose the gods' passions as mysteries. If they were going to judge us for mixing freely and indiscriminately, they ought either to hate Zeus — begotten from his mother Rhea and his daughter Kore, and taking his own sister as a wife — or to hate Orpheus, Zeus's maker, because Orpheus also made Zeus more unholy than Thyestes and defiled; for Zeus too lay with his daughter by an oracle's command, wanting to reign and take revenge. We, however, stand so far from such indifference that we are not even permitted to look with desire. For, he says, whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery in his heart (Matthew 5:28). To those to whom nothing more is allowed to be seen than what God created the eyes for — so that we may be light — and to those for whom seeing adulteries is a pleasure, because their eyes have become something other than what they were made for, until their thoughts are judged, how could these people be trusted to be self‑controlled? For our standard is not human laws, which anyone who becomes wicked can evade (indeed, from the beginning I testified to you, rulers, that the teaching among us is God‑taught), but we have a law that established a measure of righteousness for them and for those around them. Therefore we regard as sons and daughters those of like age, we have brothers and sisters, and we render to our elders the honor due fathers and mothers. Because we count as brothers and sisters and by the other family names those whom we so regard, it matters greatly to us that their bodies remain unviolated and incorrupt, for the Word again tells us: if anyone kisses a second time because it pleased him, and adding, 'Thus one must be precise about the kiss, or rather the greeting, so that, if the mind is slightly darkened, it does not put us outside eternal life.'

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex Greek syntax regarding the mythological comparisons and the Christian ethical distinctions. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the necessary scripture citation (Matthew 5:28) for the clause 'whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery in his heart', which is required by the instructions for added identifications. The translation of 'ἐπιστούμην' as 'testified/testimony' and 'ἀκριβώσασθαι' as 'be precise' is faithful to the Greek.
